facts: Multiplying a Decimal by an int keeps exact decimal precision.
Converting a Decimal to float before multiplying can introduce rounding error.
A zero amount multiplies to a zero total and must still be reported.
fact_paraphrases: An int multiplier preserves a Decimal's exact precision.
Coercing the Decimal to float before the multiplication can round the result.
Calling float on the Decimal first may lose precision.
A zero amount produces a zero total that is still reported.
